Phase 1
interlocutor
To both candidates Good morning / afternoon / evening.
Can I have your mark sheets, please?
Hand over the mark sheets to the Assessor.
I’m ......................, and this is ......................
To Candidate A What’s your name?
To Candidate B What’s your name?
Back-up prompts
B, do you work, or are
you a student?
For UK, ask Where do you come from? Are you from (Spain, etc)?
For Non-UK, ask Where do you live? Do you live in … (name of district / town, etc)?
Thank you.

a student?

Part 1 (3 - 4 minutes)

A2 Key Speaking Sample Test 2

Phase 2
interlocutor
Now, let’s talk about reading.
Back-up prompts
A, what kind of things do you read online? Do you read the news online?
How often do you read something in English? Do you sometimes read books or magazines
in English?
B, what have you read today? Have you read a newspaper today?
When do you usually read? Do you read before you go to sleep at night?
extended response Back-up questions
Now, A, please tell me about the best book What is the name of your favourite book?
you have read. Was it an exciting book?
Where do you usually get books from?
interlocutor
Now, let’s talk about where you live.
Back-up prompts
B, which sports can you play near your home? Is there a football pitch near your home?
Where can you walk to from your home? Can you walk to the centre of town from
your home?
A, where is the best place near your home Is there a café where you meet
to meet your friends? your friends?
What are the shops like near your home? Are there any good shops near your home?
extended response Back-up questions
Now, B, please tell me something about Where do you like to go out near your home?
your favourite place near your home. How often do you go there?
What can you do there?

A2 KeySpeaking Sample Test 2
© Cambridge University Press and UCLES 2019
Phase 1
interlocutor Now, in this part of the test you are going to talk together.
¸ 3–4 minutes Place Part 2 booklet, open at Task 2a, in front of candidates.
Here are some pictures that show different things you can do on a computer.
Do you like doing these different things on a computer? Say why or why not.
I’ll say that again.
Do you like doing these different things on a computer? Say why or why not.
All right? Now, talk together.
Candidates ………………………………………………………..
¸ Allow a minimum of 1 minute (maximum of 2 minutes) before moving on to
the following questions.
interlocutor / Do you think …
Candidates … reading the news on a computer is boring?
… watching videos on a computer is useful?
… looking at photos on a computer is interesting?
… listening to music on a computer is good?
… chatting to friends on a computer is fun?
interlocutor So, A, which of these things you can do on a computer do you like best?
And you, B, which of these things you can do on a computer do you like best?
Thank you. (Can I have the booklet, please?) Retrieve Part 2 booklet.
Phase 2
interlocutor Now, is it better to contact people by email or phone, B? (Why?)
¸
And what about you, A? (Is it better to contact people by email or phone?)
(Why?)
What kind of problems do people sometimes have with their computers or
mobile phones, A? (Why?)
And what about you, B? (What kind of problems do people have with their
computers or mobile phones?) (Why?)
Thank you. That is the end of the test.
Optional prompt
Why? / Why not?
What do you think?
Use as appropriate.
Ask each candidate
at least one question.
Allow up to
2 minutes
